name: Frente del Agua, Paredes de Buitrago
story: In late July 1936 rebel troops under Colonel García Escámez crossed the Somosierra and seized Paredes de Buitrago, close to the El Villar and Puentes Viejas reservoirs that supplied Madrid with water. Republican forces, helped by workers of the Canal de Isabel II who fortified the positions, stopped them just short. The front stabilised by the end of August and stayed here for the rest of the war, the Nationalist 72nd Division facing Republican mixed brigades across the valley. The Comunidad de Madrid has cleared and signposted 26 positions of both armies.
see: Trenches, machine-gun nests, shelters and command posts at Loma Quemada (Republican), El Pinar and Peñas Bajas (Nationalist), with information panels.
plan: An 8 km circular waymarked route starts from the interpretation centre in the old village laundry. Allow 3 hours; good footwear.
